page.layout: One printed page, right side of the scan. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Text block in one column with a display formula in the middle. Right margin carries only handwritten annotations, which are not transcribed. The left edge shows the neighbouring page and is excluded.

main_text.p: Compositio additionis est sumptio plurium tum antecedentium, tum consequentium simul, velut unius antecedentis ad unum consequentem.

Quanquam plures sunt additionis compositiones, qualis est σὼ θροις λόγος [?], ad 1 5 d. 5: inter eas tamen haec maxime frequens est, quare specialis haec definitio huic instituto sufficiens, generalis loco assumpta sit. Exempli gratia, si 3 ad 2 sunt, ut 9 ad 6: tum per additionis compositionem 3 & 9, id est 12, ad 2 & 6, id est 8, pariter se habebunt, sesquialtera nempe ratione. Unde termini proportionis sunt, ut vides:
In hac igitur multiplici proportione sequens Theorema valet.

p.i: Si e terminus multiplicis proportionis unius rationis consequentes additi, antecedentes autem separati dentur: tum ut antecedentes per additionem compositi ad consequentes additos sunt, ita & singuli antecedentes ad suos sigillatim consequentes erunt, & inuersè.

main_text.p: Est 12 p. 7, nisi quòd inuersè & huic proposito accommodatius paulò enunciata est. Asserit enim illa, Datis quotlibet numeris proportionalibus: quantus sit unus antecedens ad suum consequentem, tantos fore omnes

page.notes: Handwritten annotations in the right margin and at the foot of the page (including the marginal Theorema notes and the lines beginning "Regula") are manuscript and were not transcribed. The Greek word in the second paragraph is uncertain. The last printed line is partly overwritten by handwriting. Section symbols and superscript numbers in the display formula are as far as I could read them.
